theorems.name: Annuity-Due Geometric Closed Form
theorems.description: Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} v^k = (1 - v^n)/(1 - v) for v ≠ 1. The annuity-due present value formula, mirror of the immediate-annuity case.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.Insurance

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin

theorem annuityDue_closed_form_thm (v : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (hv : v ≠ 1) :
    ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, v ^ k = (1 - v ^ n) / (1 - v) :=
  MathFin.annuityDue_closed_form v n hv

metadata.reference: Annuity-due formula (Bowers et al., Actuarial Mathematics)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export from MathFin. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Gompertz Cumulative Force of Mortality
theorems.description: ∫₀^t B·e^{c·u} du = (B/c)·(e^{c·t} - 1) for c ≠ 0. The closed-form cumulative force of mortality under the Gompertz law μ(t) = B·e^{c·t}.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.Mortality

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin

theorem gompertz_cumulative_force_thm (B c t : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    ∫ u in (0:ℝ)..t, B * Real.exp (c * u) =
      (B / c) * (Real.exp (c * t) - 1) :=
  MathFin.gompertz_cumulative_force B c t hc

theorems.name: Compound-Poisson Aggregate-Loss MGF
theorems.description: For iid claim sizes Xᵢ, the MGF of the n-claim sum ∑_{i<n} Xᵢ, integrated against the Poisson(λ) law of n, equals exp(λ(M_X(t) − 1)). This is the compound-Poisson aggregate-loss MGF in mixture form: the claim count enters as the Poisson weights, not as a random variable N independent of the claims.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Probability.Jumps.CompoundPoissonMGF

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin

/-- **Compound-Poisson aggregate-loss MGF.** For a Poisson claim count `N ∼ Poisson(λ)` and
i.i.d. claim sizes `Xᵢ`, integrating the `n`-claim aggregate MGF against the Poisson law gives
`exp(λ·(M_X(t) − 1))` — the Poisson PGF evaluated at the common claim MGF. Re-exports
`MathFin.compoundPoisson_mgf`. -/
theorem compound_poisson_mgf
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
    (lam : ℝ≥0) (t : ℝ) (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
    (hindep : iIndepFun X μ)
    (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) :
    ∫ n, mgf (fun ω => ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, X i ω) μ t ∂(poissonMeasure lam)
      = Real.exp ((lam : ℝ) * (mgf (X 0) μ t - 1)) :=
  MathFin.compoundPoisson_mgf lam t X hindep hident

metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof: n-claim iid-sum MGF (iIndepFun.mgf_sum) composed with the Poisson pgf (integral_pow_poissonMeasure). Re-export from MathFin. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Compound-Poisson Aggregate-Loss MGF with a Random Claim Count
theorems.description: For a claim count N ~ Poisson(λ) independent of i.i.d. claim sizes Xᵢ with E[exp(tX₀)] finite, the aggregate loss S = ∑_{i<N} Xᵢ has E[exp(tS)] = exp(λ(M_X(t) − 1)). The count is a random variable on the same probability space as the claims; the expectation over it is computed by freezing the count, which reduces it to the mixture form mf-compound-poisson-mgf.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Probability.Jumps.CompoundPoissonMGF

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal

/-- **Compound-Poisson aggregate-loss MGF.** For `N ∼ Poisson(λ)` independent of i.i.d. claim
sizes `Xᵢ` whose MGF is finite at `t`, `𝔼[exp(t·∑_{i<N} Xᵢ)] = exp(λ·(M_X(t) − 1))`. -/
theorem compound_poisson_mgf_random_count_thm {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
    (lam : ℝ≥0) (t : ℝ) {N : Ω → ℕ} (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
    (hN : HasLaw N (poissonMeasure lam) μ) (hindep : iIndepFun X μ)
    (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ)
    (hNX : IndepFun N (fun ω i ↦ X i ω) μ)
    (hint : Integrable (fun ω ↦ Real.exp (t * X 0 ω)) μ) :
    mgf (fun ω ↦ ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N ω), X i ω) μ t
      = Real.exp ((lam : ℝ) * (mgf (X 0) μ t - 1)) :=
  MathFin.compoundPoisson_mgf_of_indepFun lam t X hN hindep hident hNX hint

metadata.reference: Compound Poisson MGF (Cramér-Lundberg actuarial theory); e.g. Klugman-Panjer-Willmot, Loss Models, Thm 9.3
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof: integrating out the independent Poisson count (integral_comp_of_hasLaw_of_countable, the freezing lemma for a countable variable), with E[exp(t·∑_{i<n} Xᵢ)] = M_X(t)ⁿ for each n (mgf_range_sum_of_iid, integrable by integrable_exp_mul_sum_range_of_iid) and n ↦ M_X(t)ⁿ integrable against Poisson(λ) (PoissonPgf.integrable_pow_poissonMeasure), then the mixture form compoundPoisson_mgf. The claim MGF must be finite at t (hint): otherwise E[exp(tS)] = +∞ when λ > 0, which the Bochner mgf records as 0, and the identity fails. Lives in MathFin/Probability/Jumps/CompoundPoissonMGF.lean, on MathFin/Probability/Analysis/IndepFreezing.lean. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Survival Ratio tpₓ = S_X(x+t)/S_X(x)
theorems.description: Keystone of the survival model (Ito's ccdfTx_ccdfX): the conditional survival probability tpₓ = P(X>x+t | X>x) equals the ratio S_X(x+t)/S_X(x) of unconditional survival probabilities, for t ≥ 0.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.SurvivalModel

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open MathFin.SurvivalModel

/-- **Survival ratio** `tpₓ = S_X(x+t) / S_X(x)` for `t ≥ 0` — the keystone of the
survival model (Ito's `ccdfTx_ccdfX`): conditioning on survival to age `x`, a further
`t` years of survival has probability the ratio of the two unconditional survival
probabilities. Re-exports `MathFin.SurvivalModel.survive_eq_survivalFunction_ratio`. -/
theorem survival_ratio
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {X : Ω → ℝ}
    (hX : Measurable X) (x : ℝ) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    survive P X t x = survivalFunction P X (x + t) / survivalFunction P X x :=
  MathFin.SurvivalModel.survive_eq_survivalFunction_ratio hX x ht

metadata.reference: Yosuke Ito, AFP Actuarial Mathematics, Survival_Model (ccdfTx_ccdfX)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof, our own design: the conditional survival probability, defined via Mathlib's conditional measure cond, collapses to the survival-function ratio through cond_apply and the sub-event alive(x+t) ⊆ alive(x). The AFP entry (Ito, Actuarial Mathematics, Survival_Model) was consulted as a source and is cited. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Survival Function at Age Zero S_X(0)=1
theorems.description: Ito's ccdfX_0_1: the survival function of the age at death is 1 at age 0, since X > 0 almost surely.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.SurvivalModel

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open MathFin.SurvivalModel

/-- **`S_X(0) = 1`**: everyone is alive at age `0`, since the age at death `X > 0`
almost surely — Ito's `ccdfX_0_1`. Re-exports `MathFin.SurvivalModel.survivalFunction_zero`. -/
theorem survival_at_zero
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {X : Ω → ℝ}
    (hpos : ∀ᵐ ω ∂P, 0 < X ω) :
    survivalFunction P X 0 = 1 :=
  MathFin.SurvivalModel.survivalFunction_zero hpos

metadata.reference: Yosuke Ito, AFP Actuarial Mathematics, Survival_Model (ccdfX_0_1)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof, our own design: X > 0 a.e. makes {X > 0} an ae-full event, so P{X>0} = 1 via measure_congr on the ae-equality to univ. The AFP entry (Ito, Actuarial Mathematics, Survival_Model) was consulted as a source and is cited. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Formalize the classical loaded premium principles (expected-value, variance, standard-deviation) and their nonnegative-loading bounds
theorems.description: Classical loaded premium principles and their nonnegative-loading bounds: each prices at or above the pure premium.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.ActuarialInsurance

open MathFin

/-- The three classical loaded premium principles with nonnegative loadings price at or above the pure premium (the mean loss). -/
theorem mf_insurance_premium_principles (μ σ2 σ θ α β : ℝ) (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (hσ2 : 0 ≤ σ2)
    (hσ : 0 ≤ σ) (hθ : 0 ≤ θ) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hβ : 0 ≤ β) :
    expectedValuePremium θ μ ≥ μ ∧ variancePremium α μ σ2 ≥ μ ∧ stdDevPremium β μ σ ≥ μ :=
  MathFin.premium_ge_mean μ σ2 σ θ α β hμ hσ2 hσ hθ hα hβ

theorems.name: Life Annuity-Due Under a Constant Force of Mortality
theorems.description: With flat-rate discount factors B(0, k) = e^{−rk} (zero-coupon bond prices) and survival probabilities S(k) = exp(−∫₀ᵏ μ) for a constant force of mortality μ ≡ m, the n-payment life annuity-due Σ_{k<n} B(0, k)·S(k) equals (1 − vⁿ)/(1 − v) with v = e^{−(r+m)}, provided v ≠ 1: a constant force of mortality acts as an addition to the interest rate. The life annuity-due is defined as this sum; its identification with the value of the payments made while a random lifetime has not ended is the entry mf-life-annuity-due-is-contract-value.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.Insurance

open MathFin

/-- Under a constant force of mortality `m`, the life annuity-due is the annuity-certain at the
discount factor `e^{−(r + m)}`. -/
theorem life_annuity_due_constant_force_thm {r m : ℝ} (n : ℕ)
    (hv : Real.exp (-(r + m)) ≠ 1) :
    lifeAnnuityDue r (fun _ ↦ m) n =
      (1 - Real.exp (-(r + m)) ^ n) / (1 - Real.exp (-(r + m))) :=
  lifeAnnuityDue_const n hv

metadata.reference: D. C. M. Dickson, M. R. Hardy and H. R. Waters, Actuarial Mathematics for Life Contingent Risks, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press (2013), Chapter 5 (annuities)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.lifeAnnuityDue_const (MathFin/Insurance/Insurance.lean). lifeAnnuityDue r μ n := Σ_{k<n} zcb r 0 k · survivalFromForce μ k, with zcb from MathFin/Models/Rates/ZCB.lean and survivalFromForce from MathFin/Insurance/Mortality.lean; the closed form is the annuity-due geometric sum annuityDue_closed_form at v = e^{−(r+m)}. SCOPE: constant force of mortality and flat rate; the probabilistic reading of the sum as the value of payments to a random lifetime is lifeAnnuityDue_eq_value (MathFin/Insurance/AnnuityValue.lean), a separate entry.

theorems.name: The Life Annuity-Due Is the Value of Payments Made While the Default Indicator of the Lifetime Is Zero
theorems.description: Let tau be a measurable lifetime under a probability measure Q whose survival probabilities S_tau(k) = Q(tau > k) at the dates k < n are those of a force of mortality mu, survivalFromForce mu k. Then the life annuity-due of n payments, the sum over k < n of the flat-rate zero-coupon bond price zcb r 0 k times survivalFromForce mu k (lifeAnnuityDue), is the value (Contract.value) under Q, on the deterministic flat-rate discount t -> zcb r 0 t, of the contract that pays one at each date k < n while the default indicator 1{tau <= k} of the lifetime is still zero (the schedule of payments payFlows of 1 - 1{tau <= k}). The value is under the law of the lifetime: no market is involved, and the survival probabilities at the other dates are not used.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.AnnuityValue

open MeasureTheory MathFin MathFin.Contracts
open scoped NNReal

/-- The life annuity-due is the value, on the flat-rate discount, of the payments of one made
while the default indicator of the lifetime is zero. -/
theorem life_annuity_due_is_contract_value {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} (Q : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
    {τ : Ω → ℝ} (hτ : Measurable τ) (r : ℝ) (μ : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ)
    (hS : ∀ k < n, SurvivalModel.survivalFunction Q τ k = survivalFromForce μ k) :
    lifeAnnuityDue r μ n =
      (payFlows (fun k ↦ (k : ℝ≥0)) (fun k ↦ (.sub (.const 1) (.obs () k) : Payoff Unit)) n).value
        Q (fun t _ ↦ zcb r 0 t) (defaultIndicator τ) :=
  lifeAnnuityDue_eq_value Q hτ r μ n hS

metadata.reference: D. C. M. Dickson, M. R. Hardy and H. R. Waters, Actuarial Mathematics for Life Contingent Risks, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press (2013), Chapter 5 (annuities)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof of the statement as written. lifeAnnuityDue_eq_value in MathFin/Insurance/AnnuityValue.lean: along every scenario the schedule is worth the sum of the discounted payoffs (pathPV_payFlows), the integral of the sum is the sum of the integrals, and the integral of 1 - 1{tau <= k} is 1 - Q(tau <= k), which is the survival function at k (probReal_compl_eq_one_sub); the contract is the one of the credit module (defaultIndicator, Models/Credit/DefaultTime.lean). SCOPE: a deterministic discount and a lifetime under Q; the identification is for the dates k < n at which the survival function is that of the force of mortality. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: The Esscher Premium Is the Price of the Loss Under the Esscher Pricing Measure of the Insured Market
theorems.description: Let X be a measurable loss under a probability measure P with e^(hX) and X e^(hX) integrable. In the insured market (insuredMarket: the one-date market with the unit numeraire in which the loss is quoted at its Esscher premium E[X e^(hX)] / E[e^(hX)] until the date T and equals X at T), the Esscher tilt of P with density e^(hX)/E[e^(hX)] is a pricing measure (Market.IsPricingMeasure at T), and under it the market's price (Market.price) of the claim paying the loss at T is the Esscher premium E[X e^(hX)] / E[e^(hX)]. The market is built to quote the loss at that premium and has no dynamics before T. For an arbitrary market with the unit numeraire the same price identity holds for the claim paying the asset at T under the Esscher tilt of its reference measure (esscherPremium_eq_price).

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.EsscherPremium

open MeasureTheory MathFin MathFin.Contracts
open scoped NNReal

/-- The Esscher tilt is a pricing measure of the insured market, and under it the loss is worth
the Esscher premium. -/
theorem esscher_premium_is_price {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {X : Ω → ℝ}
    (hX : Measurable X) {h : ℝ} (hexp : Integrable (fun ω ↦ Real.exp (h * X ω)) P)
    (hXexp : Integrable (fun ω ↦ X ω * Real.exp (h * X ω)) P) (T : ℝ≥0) :
    (insuredMarket P hX h T).IsPricingMeasure T (P.tilted fun ω ↦ h * X ω) ∧
      (insuredMarket P hX h T).price (P.tilted fun ω ↦ h * X ω) (.pay T (.obs () T))
        = (∫ ω, X ω * Real.exp (h * X ω) ∂P) / ∫ ω, Real.exp (h * X ω) ∂P :=
  ⟨isPricingMeasure_insuredMarket_tilted hX hexp hXexp T, price_insuredMarket_tilted hX T⟩

metadata.reference: Gerber and Shiu, Option pricing by Esscher transforms (1994); Esscher, On the probability function in the collective theory of risk (1932)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof of the statement as written. isPricingMeasure_insuredMarket_tilted and price_insuredMarket_tilted in MathFin/Insurance/EsscherPremium.lean, on the one-date market Market.oneDate (MathFin/Pricing/OneDateMarket.lean) with its initial price the Esscher premium: the tilt is a probability measure equivalent to P (isProbabilityMeasure_tilted, tilted_absolutelyContinuous, absolutelyContinuous_tilted), X is integrable under it (integrable_tilted_iff) with mean the premium (integral_tilted_eq_esscherPremium), and a measure with those properties prices the one-date market (Market.isPricingMeasure_oneDate). The general price identity for an arbitrary market with unit numeraire is esscherPremium_eq_price in the same module. SCOPE: the insured market quotes the loss at the Esscher premium by construction, and there is no dynamics before T; the statement does not derive the premium from a hedging or equilibrium argument. Axioms-clean.
